TriGParserCustomTest#testParseTruePrefix.spec: RDF 1.2 TriG section 4.5 (grammar [PNAME_LN], [PN_PREFIX]) and RDF 1.2 Turtle section 6 note 3: "When tokenizing the input and choosing grammar rules, the longest match is chosen."
TriGParserCustomTest#testParseTruePrefix.note: In object position the lexer reads 'true'/'false' as BooleanLiteral even when ':' follows, so true:o (a PNAME_LN, the longest match) is refused with 'expected . after triple'. Subject and predicate positions accept true:s / true:p; truex:o is accepted. Same in turtle, trig, trig12.

TriGParserCustomTest#testDirLangStringNo.spec: RDF 1.2 Concepts section 3.3 (Literals: the datatype IRI is rdf:dirLangString if and only if the literal has a language tag and a base direction); W3C rdf-tests rdf12 ntriples-langdir-bad-5 is a negative syntax test of the same literal
TriGParserCustomTest#testDirLangStringNo.note: RDF4J (VERIFY_DATATYPE_VALUES=false, its default) rewrites "Hello"^^rdf:dirLangString with no language tag to the xsd:string literal "Hello"; Factoidal refuses it (term.invalid-langtag).
